slides.text: run and lift? don't treat them as separate
save this. you'll need it at the gym
strength training helps your stability, leg strength, joint durability, and injury prevention. it's not just building muscle, it's building a body that runs more efficiently for longer.
but the problem starts when you train with no plan. heavy legs before a speed session or a long run = you're running gassed.

get a lifting plan that adjusts around your sport
try the app
keep heavy leg days away from your hard or long runs. days close to running should be lighter. focused on movement and stability.
squats, lunges, RDLs, and calf/core work help a ton, just pick the right weight and keep your form clean.
the goal is for lifting to make you stronger for running, not slower or heavier-legged.
